# TextArea

Figma: [03n. TextArea](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-909) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-26

Multi-line text input with auto-expanding height and a vertical resize handle. The TextArea family covers three patterns: the bare Field atom (just the input box), the full TextArea organism (Label + Field + Helper + character counter), and the TextArea Underline (minimal underline-only style for dense contexts). Use for deal descriptions, investor notes, comments, KYC justifications, document descriptions, and any input that needs more than a single line.

### TextArea Field

The bare bordered multi-line input box with auto-expand and a vertical resize handle, without label or helper.

Level: atom · Part of: TextArea

Use when:
- The field slot inside TextArea or a Form Field
- Custom layouts that compose their own label

Don't use when:
- A labelled multi-line field with counter: use TextArea
- Single-line text: use Input Field
- Notes inside dense tables: use TextArea Underline

Accessibility: Needs an external label; cap growth with max lines so pasted text does not break the layout.

### TextArea

A labelled multi-line text field with helper and optional character counter, for descriptions and justifications.

Level: organism · Contains: TextArea Field

Use when:
- Source of funds explanation in KYC
- Support or complaint messages
- Deal descriptions with a length limit: Show Counter on

Don't use when:
- Single-line answers: use Input
- Inline notes in dense admin tables: use TextArea Underline
- No real character limit: turn Show Counter off

Accessibility: Validate length on blur or submit, not per keystroke, and announce the counter when near the limit.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

### TextArea Underline

A minimal multi-line input with only a bottom underline, for notes that should recede inside dense layouts.

Level: atom · Part of: TextArea

Use when:
- Internal notes on transaction or investor rows in the back office
- Inline annotations where a column header provides context

Don't use when:
- Primary user-facing forms: use TextArea
- Needs a box border: use TextArea Field

Accessibility: Pair the red error underline with Form Field Helper text.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

TextArea is the multi-line text input - distinct from Input, which is single-line only. Use a TextArea anytime users need to type a description, justification, narrative, or any content that benefits from line breaks. The field auto-expands as the user types and offers a vertical resize handle for manual height adjustment.

Common Safqah use cases: deal description (issuer drafts a 200–500 char summary), investor justification ("Why I'm increasing my commitment"), KYC additional info ("Source of funds explanation"), document description (when uploading compliance docs), internal admin notes on transactions, and email/announcement composition. The character counter helps users stay within copy length budgets - important for content that flows into a fixed-width card or a summary view.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Three components covering the spectrum from minimum to maximum. Same input semantics; different visual chrome and composition.

Atom - TextArea Field · 36 variants

The bare multi-line input box. Border on all four sides, auto-expanding height, vertical resize handle in the bottom corner (LTR = bottom-right, RTL = bottom-left). Variants: 3 sizes × 6 states × 2 directions. Use inside Form Field organisms via INSTANCE_SWAP or compose manually with your own label/helper.

Organism - TextArea · 30 variants

Full composition with Label above + exposed Field slot in the middle + bottom row (Helper text on one side, character counter on the other). Variants: 3 sizes × 5 states × 2 directions. The Field instance is exposed for swap - designers can replace the bare Field with a different Field variant (e.g., Underline style) without rebuilding the wrapper.

Style variant - TextArea Underline · 36 variants

Minimal style with just a bottom underline - no box border, no background fill. Used in dense admin tables, inline annotations, internal notes on transaction rows, and "tertiary" inputs where the full box chrome would feel heavy. Variants: 3 sizes × 6 states × 2 directions.

### Sizes

Three sizes for different content density. Padding, font, and minimum height scale together.

Large (16dp font, 120dp min height)

Primary inputs - deal descriptions, investor justifications, KYC narratives. Mobile-first. Generous padding for thumb-friendly editing.

Medium (14dp font, 96dp min height)

Standard desktop density - admin notes, transaction descriptions, internal comments. Most common for desktop UIs.

Small (12dp font, 80dp min height)

Compact contexts - inline edit cells, dense admin tables, audit log annotations. Avoid for primary user input.

### States

Five states cover the input lifecycle. Each state propagates from the Field atom up through the TextArea organism to the visible Helper tone and counter color.

default

Empty resting state. Placeholder text in muted color, default border, helper showing static field guidance, counter at "0 / max".

filled

User has typed content. Value displayed in default text color, multi-line wrap, counter shows current character count.

focus

Field is active. Border switches to border/focus (2dp dark), helper still visible. Picker dialogs don't apply (typed input, no popover).

error

Validation failed. Border switches to red, helper shows error message with alert icon, counter switches to red. Pair with concrete error copy (e.g., "Please enter at least 50 characters" or "Maximum 500 characters exceeded").

disabled

Field is inert. Reduced opacity background (bg/disabled), muted value text, helper hidden. Resize handle hidden. Use when content is system-determined (e.g., a read-only audit note).

### Direction - LTR and RTL

TextArea flips internal alignment for Arabic. Label aligned right, value text right-aligned, resize handle moves to the bottom-left corner (visually leading edge), and the bottom row swaps positions - character counter on the LEFT (leading edge in RTL), helper on the RIGHT.

LTR

English / default. Label aligned left, value text left-aligned. Resize handle at bottom-right (trailing edge). Bottom row: helper on the LEFT, counter on the RIGHT. Character counter format: "342 / 500".

RTL

Arabic. Label aligned right ("وصف الصفقة"), value text right-aligned. Resize handle at bottom-LEFT (visually leading edge in RTL = trailing in reading order, but visual = leading). Bottom row: counter on the LEFT, helper on the RIGHT.

> **Tip:** Numbers in the character counter (342 / 500) use Arabic-Indic numerals (٣٤٢ / ٥٠٠) when the field is in RTL mode in actual Safqah product. The Figma counter shows Western numerals here as a simplification - runtime framework code switches numeral system based on locale.

### Underline style - when minimal beats boxed

TextArea Underline is the minimal variant: no box border, no background fill, just a bottom underline. Use it when the full boxed input would feel heavy - inside dense admin tables, inline annotations on transaction rows, internal notes that should visually recede.

The underline pattern follows the same Size × State × Direction matrix as the regular Field. State transitions (hover / focus / error) change the underline color and weight but never restore the box border - the visual restraint is the point. If you find yourself wanting a box border on the underline variant, switch to the regular TextArea Field instead.

Filled - investment note

Typed annotation on a transaction row. Underline maintains visual hierarchy without competing with the row chrome.

Focus - active editing

Underline darkens to 2dp focus weight. No box appears - keeps the visual restraint of the resting state.

Error - validation failure

Underline turns red. Pair with a Form Field Helper below explaining the specific failure.

### Code examples

How to consume TextArea components in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic TextArea with character counter

```dart
// Full TextArea organism - label + field + helper + counter
class _DealDescriptionFieldState extends State<DealDescriptionField> {
  final _controller = TextEditingController();
  static const _maxLength = 500;
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return SafqahTextArea(
      label: 'Deal description',
      isRequired: true,
      controller: _controller,
      placeholder: 'Describe your deal - include key terms, sector, and expected returns...',
      maxLength: _maxLength,
      minLines: 4,
      maxLines: 10,
      helperText: 'Brief description of the deal key terms',
      // Error state triggered if length < 50 on submit
      validator: (text) => (text?.length ?? 0) < 50
        ? 'Please enter at least 50 characters'
        : null,
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - Underline variant for inline annotation

```dart
// Underline TextArea - minimal style for inline notes on transactions
class _TransactionNoteState extends State<TransactionNote> {
  final _controller = TextEditingController();
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return SafqahTextAreaUnderline(
      controller: _controller,
      placeholder: 'Add notes about this commitment...',
      minLines: 2,
      maxLines: 5,
      // No label, no helper - meant to feel inline with the row
      // Saves on space in dense tables and audit views
      onChanged: (text) {
        widget.onNoteChange(text);
      },
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - Arabic RTL context

```dart
// Arabic locale - TextArea flips internally
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahTextArea(
    label: 'وصف الصفقة',  // "Deal description"
    isRequired: true,
    controller: _controller,
    placeholder: 'صف الصفقة - اذكر الشروط الرئيسية، القطاع، والعوائد المتوقعة...',
    maxLength: 500,
    minLines: 4,
    helperText: 'وصف مختصر لشروط الصفقة الرئيسية',
    validator: (text) => (text?.length ?? 0) < 50
      ? 'يرجى إدخال وصف لا يقل عن 50 حرفاً'
      : null,
  ),
)
```

### Flutter - using inside a Form Field wrapper

```dart
// Wrap a bare TextArea Field in a Form Field for advanced layouts
SafqahFormField(
  label: 'Additional notes',
  tooltip: 'Optional - include any context relevant to the deal',
  inputSlot: SafqahTextAreaField(
    controller: _notesController,
    placeholder: 'Add any additional context...',
    minLines: 3,
    maxLines: 8,
  ),
  state: FormFieldState.defaultState,
  helperText: 'Up to 1000 characters',
  helperTone: HelperTone.neutral,
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Deal description on a creation form: Use the full TextArea organism for the deal description field. Include label, placeholder, character counter (max 500), and helper text. Required field - show red asterisk. Auto-expand from 4 to 10 lines. Helper explains scope: "Brief description of the deal key terms".
- **Don't** · Deal description on a creation form: Don't use an Input organism (single-line) and just make it taller. Don't use a bare TextArea Field without label/helper - users need context for what to write. Don't hide the character counter - users need to know about the 500-char budget BEFORE they write 800 characters.
- **Do** · Inline annotation on a transaction row: Use the TextArea Underline variant - no box border, just an underline. Auto-expand from 2 to 5 lines. No label needed (the table column header serves as context). Saves vertical space in dense admin tables. Underline darkens on focus, turns red on error.
- **Don't** · Inline annotation on a transaction row: Don't use the full boxed TextArea inside dense tables - it adds too much visual weight, fights with the row chrome, and pushes the table height up. Don't use an Input organism instead (single-line) - admin notes often need 2-3 lines.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL deal narrative: RTL direction. Label aligned right ("وصف الصفقة"), value text right-aligned with Arabic text wrapping correctly. Resize handle moves to bottom-left. Bottom row: counter on LEFT (visually leading edge), helper on RIGHT. Error copy in Arabic: "يرجى إدخال وصف لا يقل عن 50 حرفاً".
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL deal narrative: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts - Arabic text left-aligned with LTR layout looks broken. Don't mix English placeholders with Arabic-only forms. Don't use Western numerals in the character counter for Arabic mode if your runtime supports Arabic-Indic numerals (٣٤٢ / ٥٠٠).
- **Do** · Character limit validation: Use the error state when the user submits with too few/too many characters. Border + helper + counter all turn red. Helper shows the specific constraint: "Please enter at least 50 characters" or "Maximum 500 characters exceeded". The counter visually emphasizes the overflow.
- **Don't** · Character limit validation: Don't leave the field in default state after a failed submit. Don't use a toast or top-banner error for inline length validation - anchored inline feedback is more actionable. Don't pre-validate on every keystroke for "too few" - let the user finish writing; validate on blur or submit.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** TextArea is the single-purpose multi-line companion to Input. They share most chrome (border, focus state, error state, padding, label/helper composition) but differ on: multi-line height, auto-expand behavior, vertical resize handle, and the optional character counter. If you find yourself wanting a "tall single-line input" for free text - use TextArea, not Input with a manual resize.

> **Tip:** The character counter is OPTIONAL at the framework level (toggle via the Show Counter boolean prop on the TextArea organism). Use it when there's a real maxLength constraint (e.g., the value flows into a 500-char card preview). DON'T use it cosmetically - a counter without a meaningful limit creates anxiety without purpose.

> **Info:** The Underline variant intentionally does NOT include a Label/Helper organism wrapper - the whole point is the visual restraint. If you need a label above an Underline field, compose it manually with Form Field Label + the Underline atom. The full Underline organism would defeat the purpose.

> **Warning:** Auto-expand behavior - the field grows to fit content but caps at maxLines (default 10 for lg, 8 for md, 6 for sm). Beyond the cap, the field starts scrolling internally. Don't set maxLines to infinity - it breaks page layouts when users paste 5000 words of LLM-generated text.

> **Warning:** Resize handle limitation - Figma can't simulate the actual drag-to-resize behavior in a static component. The handle here is a visual indicator only. The runtime framework code (Flutter / React) provides the actual resize cursor and drag handling. Test the resize affordance in the live app, not in Figma.

> **Warning:** BOOLEAN property defaultValue gotcha hit again (locked constraint #13). Show Helper boolean on the TextArea organism initially took its default from the first variant's value (false), overriding per-variant visibility. Workaround: removed componentPropertyReferences.visible from the Helper instance on each variant, set helper.visible directly based on the state axis. Same fix pattern as FormField organism.

> **Warning:** RTL implementation hits locked constraint #11 (TEXT property defaultValue takes from first variant). Workaround: removed componentPropertyReferences.characters on RTL variants and set Arabic text directly. Filled-state variants in LTR also needed direct text setting since the placeholder/filled text differ. Same as TextArea Underline.

> **Info:** Character counter format - defaults to "X / Y" where X is current and Y is max. Some products show "Y - X remaining" instead (e.g. "158 remaining"). The current/max format is more conventional but the remaining format better signals when users are close to the limit. If product research shows the remaining format is clearer for Safqah users, switch - but make it consistent across the app.

> **Info:** Vertical-only resize - the handle resizes height only, never width. Allowing horizontal resize would let users break page layouts (especially in grid systems). If a TextArea needs to be wider, that's a design-time decision via the wrapping container width, not a runtime user choice.

> **Info:** Disabled state hides the resize handle - when the field is inert, no point showing the resize affordance. The disabled background (bg/disabled) signals "you can't edit this" and the missing handle reinforces "you can't resize either".

> **Tip:** WCAG considerations - minimum touch target for resize handle on mobile should be ≥ 24dp drag area (even if the visual icon is 12dp). The hover/focus state on the handle should be visually distinguishable from the resting state. The lockup of resize ergonomics is delegated to runtime framework (Flutter GestureDetector / web cursor:nwse-resize).

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the form family. All text uses IBM Plex Sans Regular/Medium/SemiBold. Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, and Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.
